lots.title: Inspection & Maintenance of Indoor Gymnasium, Fitness & Sport Equipment and Outdoor Schools Play & Sport Equipment
lots.description: ESPO Framework Agreement 107_26 template (Appendix A) for the provision of inspection and maintenance of indoor gymnasium, fitness & sport equipment and outdoor schools play & sport equipment to ESPO customers (public bodies in England and potentially the wider UK). This document is the legal framework template only; Schedule 1 (The Goods and/or Services) is a stub that will be populated post-award by incorporating the Specification from Section 2 of the Invitation to Tender and the Supplier's Statement of Requirements response from the Tender Submission Document, neither of which is contained in this document. The Commencement Date is 09 June 2026; Initial Term is 20 Months with optional extensions up to 28 additional Months. Customers may call off either without competition (e.g. cheapest Supplier at Framework Prices) or via Further Competitive Selection Process. Clause 26.16 (Partial Termination) confirms the framework contains Lots, but no lot-level breakdown is made visible in this Framework Agreement template — the lot structure, Goods/Services detail, quantities, CPV split and technical specifications must be read from the separately issued Specification pack.
requirements: Enter into Contracts with Customers in accordance with the Framework Schedule 4 Ordering Procedure, on the terms of the Form of Contract, Master Contract Schedule and Call-Off Terms (clauses 6.1, 6.2).
Ensure any Goods supplied to Customers conform to the Specification and the Call-Off Terms (clause 7.5).

Perform all obligations under Contracts in accordance with the Framework Agreement, Good Industry Practice, with appropriately experienced, qualified and trained personnel, with all due skill, care and diligence, and in compliance with all applicable Law (clauses 12.1.1-12.1.5).

Comply with the Standards (British Standards, international standards, ESPO's internal policies and procedures, Government codes of practice and guidance) referred to in Framework Schedule 1 in performing obligations (clause 13.2, 'Standards' definition).
Obtain and maintain all licences, authorisations, consents or permits required in relation to performance of obligations (clause 13.1).
Meet or exceed the Key Performance Indicators set out in Annex A of Framework Schedule 10 at all times (clause 7.1.11, Schedule 10 Annex A).

Submit full, accurate and complete MI Reports to ESPO Quarterly using the MI Reporting Template, by the 5th Working Day after each Quarter, until all Contracts have permanently ceased (Framework Schedule 7 paragraphs 2.1, 3.1, 3.3).
Pay the Framework Fee of 3.5% to ESPO within 30 days of ESPO's invoice, calculated Quarterly from Management Information (Framework Schedule 2 paragraphs 1.4-1.5, clauses 16.1-16.8).

Comply with anti-slavery and human trafficking laws (Modern Slavery Act 2015) and with ESPO's Conduct Policy; include equivalent provisions in sub-contracts; implement Supplier's Staff training and record-keeping (clauses 12.3.1-12.3.5).

Comply with all applicable environmental Law (including GHG Emissions, waste disposal, hazardous/toxic materials) for operations, manufactured goods and packaging; maintain an environmental management system that assesses impact, reduces emissions/pollution/waste, minimises raw materials and trains Staff (clauses 12.4-12.5).

On each anniversary of the Commencement Date, submit to ESPO a written report on GHG Emissions (using current government conversion factors) and overall sustainability impact of Framework performance (clause 12.7).
Comply with the Supplier Code of Conduct and promote Social Value in accordance with the Social Value Act 2012 and the current National Procurement Policy Statement (clauses 12.9, 12.10).

Carry out Disclosure & Barring Service enhanced checks (including Children's Barred List checks where applicable) for Supplier's Personnel or volunteers working in Regulated Activity with children and/or vulnerable adults; renew checks every three years; do not employ barred persons (clauses 13.3-13.6).
Carry out Employment Checks and DBS-required checks for Staff/volunteers who may have contact with children and/or vulnerable adults even outside Regulated Activity (clause 13.7).

Do not unlawfully discriminate within the scope of Equality Legislation (Equality Act 2010); take reasonable steps so that Staff observe this obligation; ensure written information produced under this Framework is as accessible as reasonably possible to people with disabilities (clauses 14.1, 14.2, 14.6).

Not commit any Prohibited Act, Fraud or offence under the Bribery Act 2010 in connection with this Framework Agreement; take all reasonable steps in accordance with Good Industry Practice to prevent Fraud by Supplier or Staff; comply with ESPO's published bribery/corruption policies (clauses 9.1-9.3, 11.1).

Keep and maintain, for the Term and 6 Years after termination/expiry, full and accurate records and accounts (including supply chain records) and afford ESPO and its Auditors access to these records and to Supplier Staff as requested (clauses 17.1-17.4).

Comply with Data Protection Legislation (UK GDPR, Data Protection Act 2018, PECR) as Controller; exchange only limited Personal Data as necessary; enter into a data processing agreement if any subsequent processing on behalf of ESPO arises (clauses 21.1-21.6).

Transfer all Requests for Information under FOIA/EIR to ESPO within 5 Working Days and provide all relevant Information and assistance for ESPO to respond within FOIA/EIR time limits; do not respond directly without ESPO's authorisation (clauses 22.2, 22.4).

Not make any press announcements or publicise the Framework without ESPO's Approval; undertake marketing of the Framework and Goods/Services in accordance with Framework Schedule 8 (clauses 23.1, 23.4).

Ensure that the availability, provision and use of Goods/Services does not infringe any third-party Intellectual Property Rights; hold or obtain valid licences for all IPR required for performance; indemnify ESPO against IPR infringement claims (clauses 25.2-25.4).

Take steps in accordance with Good Industry Practice to prevent introduction of viruses, worms, Trojans, spyware or other malware into systems, data or software owned by or used by ESPO and/or Customers (clause 25.3.2).

Implement a policy of continuous improvement for Goods/Services with a view to reducing ESPO and Customer costs and improving quality/efficiency; review regularly with ESPO (Framework Schedule 6 paragraph 3.1).

Provide a benchmark report on request during Benchmark Reviews, covering products/rates identified by ESPO, methodology, comparison items, market intelligence, Supplier's benchmarked rates, and competitiveness analysis (Framework Schedule 6 paragraphs 2.2.1-2.2.3).

Appoint a suitably qualified Framework Manager and a deputy, and put in place a management structure to deliver the Framework in accordance with Schedule 1 and against the Service Levels and KPIs in Schedule 10 Annex A (Framework Schedule 10 paragraphs 2.1.1, 2.1.2).

Attend Framework Review Meetings held every 12 Months (frequency/timing set by ESPO), covering strategic matters (supply chain performance, efficiency, benchmarking, market, policy, risk) and operational matters (KPI compliance, incidents, customer satisfaction, new products, environmental initiatives) (Framework Schedule 10 paragraphs 2.2.1-2.2.4).
Resolve 100% of customer complaints with an initial response within two Working Days, and 98% of complaints within ten Working Days (Framework Schedule 10 Annex A KPI row 'Complaints Resolution').
Ensure that no less than three Quarterly MI Reports are returned correct and on time by the Reporting Date in each Contract Year (Framework Schedule 10 Annex A KPI row 'Return of MI Reports').

Maintain accuracy of contact information provided to ESPO with no more than one discrepancy identified in any one Contract Year (Framework Schedule 10 Annex A KPI row 'Update of information to ESPO').
Ensure that 98% of invoices issued in every Month are accurate in amount (Framework Schedule 10 Annex A KPI row 'Invoicing').
Deliver Social Value as per each Contract, measure and report financial and non-financial benefits delivered to Customers to ESPO (Framework Schedule 10 Annex A KPI row 'Social Value').

At termination or expiry, return all ESPO Confidential Information in possession within 10 Working Days (retaining only Personal Data for compliance periods) and cooperate with access to data/information for up to 12 Months after termination (clauses 28.2, 28.3).
Pay interest on any late payments of the Framework Fee in accordance with the Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998 (clause 16.7).

warnings.message: Framework Schedule 1 (The Goods and/or Services) is a stub in this Appendix A Framework Agreement template; it refers out to the separately issued Specification (Section 2 of the Invitation to Tender) and to the Supplier's Statement of Requirements response, neither of which is contained in this document. Clause 26.16 (Partial Termination) explicitly refers to multiple 'Lots', and the title names two distinct equipment families (indoor gymnasium/fitness/sport vs outdoor schools play/sport), which strongly suggests a two-lot structure. However, the Framework Agreement text itself never labels 'Lot 1' / 'Lot 2' boundaries, so this extraction conservatively records a single lot matching the title and the existing notice-level lot record. Downstream should cross-reference the ITT Specification document (not in scope here) before treating this as a final lot structure.
evidence_refs: FRAMEWORK SCHEDULE 1 - THE GOODS AND/OR SERVICES (page 56; stub)

warnings.message: Framework Schedule 5 (Further Competitive Selection Process Award Criteria) does not enumerate specific criteria names, definitions, or weightings in this Framework Agreement template. It only states Customers 'may adopt a scheme similar to that used by ESPO' or 'advise Suppliers that a revised scheme will be used', and that increased weighting may be given to 'price' at call-off. No price/quality split is given. Framework-award evaluation criteria likely sit in the ITT (not in scope of this document).

Technical specification content (required equipment catalogues, inspection frequencies, response SLAs, specific BS EN standards, equipment categories) is not reproduced in this Framework Agreement template. Schedule 1 contains only the contractual wrapper and explicitly states it will be incorporated with the Specification (Section 2 of the ITT) and the Supplier's Statement of Requirements response post-award.
evidence_refs: Framework Schedule 1 final paragraph before Schedule 2 (page 57)

warnings.message: No CPV codes are printed in this Framework Agreement template. The process-context CPV codes held by the daemon (37400000-2 Sports goods and equipment; 50000000-5 Repair and maintenance services) have been used as CPV hints on product requirement seeds but are NOT recorded at the lot level because they are not cited in this document. Downstream should defer to the notice-level CPV.

The 'Standards' definition is generic — it references British Standards (BSI Group), international standards, ESPO's internal policies and procedures, and Government codes of practice 'referred to in Framework Schedule 1'. No specific BS EN numbers (e.g. BS EN 1176, BS EN 1177 for play equipment; BS EN 957 for fitness equipment) are named in this document. Specific standards are expected to be listed in the Specification.

The KPI table in Framework Schedule 10 Annex A covers service-management KPIs (complaints handling, MI reporting, contact accuracy, invoicing accuracy, Social Value delivery) rather than technical inspection/maintenance performance KPIs (e.g. first-time-fix rate, mean time to repair). Technical performance KPIs are referenced conceptually in paragraph 2.2.4 but are not quantified in this document.
